Thanks — quick thoughts below. I pasted the customer's redline excerpts and added our take.

> Customer: "Auto-renew shall be for a period of twelve (12) months unless Customer provides at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice."
Our take: 12-month auto-renew is ok, but we need to keep standard 30-day opt-out window tied to invoice cycle. No issue offering 12-month term if they commit to the annual seat/commit. Trade: in return we should retain the right to switch to a 12-month billing cadence (no monthly proration edge case).

> Customer: "Vendor shall ensure physical and logical segregation of Customer data in Dedicated deployments and provide vendor attestations upon request."
Our take: "attestations" is slippery. We can offer a SOC2 + written description of network segmentation as a deliverable, and for on-prem/VPC options we can agree to customer-run attestation checklists. We should avoid open-ended third-party attestations on demand (cost). Suggest: commit to documentation and 30-day response SLA for evidence requests; add a paid professional services path for custom attestations.

> Customer: "If Redwood fails to meet Latency SLO for more than two (2) consecutive days, Customer is entitled to a rollback credit equal to 10% of monthly fees per day beyond the two-day period."
Our take: credit language needs caps (monthly cap and objective measurement). Suggest we propose: credits start after three consecutive days, maximum of 25% of monthly invoice per incident, and credits calculated against documented end-to-end median P95 tail, subject to normalizing traffic anomalies. Also push for exclusion for customer-caused outages and maintenance windows.

Operational asks: Monica — can you re-run the OrderForm_Q3_Uplift numbers with the 2.5x usage and show expected monthly invoice + a pro forma credit cap (25%) so sales can see worst-case exposure? Aditya — can you sketch a short legal-friendly exhibit bullet that we can attach saying: "Evidence Request Process and Attestation Options" and flag where PS pricing applies.

I can draft the counter language tonight. Priya — if we present a clear trade (12-month auto-renew + defined credit cap + evidence process + PS path), I think Cloudfab will accept quickly.

—Ben

James / Cloudfab legal — thanks for the redlines and the clear timeline. We reviewed your asks and attached a consolidated response: 1) an annotated MSA with suggested language, 2) an updated order form reflecting the Q3 2.5x uplift, and 3) a short "Evidence & Attestation" exhibit that outlines what we can provide as standard vs. paid options.

Summary of our position (high level):
- Auto-renew: happy to move to a 12-month renewal term with a 30-day notice window tied to the annual billing cycle. (We kept language to avoid mid-period proration ambiguity.)
- Data segregation / attestations: we will provide SOC 2 report access and a standard technical segregation statement for Dedicated pools. For custom attestations, we can run a paid professional services engagement; we included an example PS price band in the exhibit. We also commit to a 30-day response SLT for routine evidence requests.
- SLA credits: we propose credits begin after three (3) consecutive days of verified latency SLO breach, credits capped at 25% of that month's invoice per incident, and exclusions for force majeure, customer-caused load spikes, and scheduled maintenance. We included objective measurement language referencing our telemetry dashboard and a normalization clause for known traffic anomalies.

Attachments: [Attachment: MSA_Annotated_Proposed.docx (docx, 68KB)], [Attachment: OrderForm_Q3_Uplift.xlsx (xlsx, 36KB)]
